root_cause.text: The error handling paths in bpf_prog_test_run_xdp() skip the xdp_convert_buff_to_md() call, which fails to release the network device reference count acquired by xdp_convert_md_to_buff().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes three error goto statements from `goto out;` to `goto out_put_dev;` and adds a new `out_put_dev:` label before the xdp_convert_buff_to_md() call. The commit message explicitly states that xdp_convert_md_to_buff() obtains a refcount that must be released by xdp_convert_buff_to_md(), and the error handling path introduced by commit 1c1949982524 "forgot to call xdp_convert_buff_to_md()" when handling memory allocation failures (MAX_SKB_FRAGS exceeded, alloc_page failure, copy_from_user failure).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by ensuring device reference is released on fragment allocation errors in XDP test run.
intent_record.what: Changed two `goto out;` statements to `goto out_put_dev;` in the bpf_prog_test_run_xdp function's error handling paths (lines 1366 and 1372).
intent_record.how: This change redirects error exit paths to a different cleanup label that properly releases a device reference before returning. Previously, errors in fragment allocation would skip device cleanup, causing a resource leak. Now both error conditions jump to out_put_dev which ensures the device is put before exiting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix resource leak by ensuring device reference is released on copy_from_user() failure in XDP test run path.
intent_record.what: Changed the goto label from 'out' to 'out_put_dev' in the error path of the copy_from_user() failure handler within the bpf_prog_test_run_xdp() function.
intent_record.how: This change alters the cleanup path taken when copying user data fails. Instead of jumping to the 'out' label, execution now jumps to 'out_put_dev', which presumably performs additional cleanup (likely releasing a device reference) before exiting. This prevents a resource leak where a device reference would not be properly released on this error condition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add cleanup label to ensure netdevice reference counting is properly decremented on all code paths including error cases.
intent_record.what: Added a label 'out_put_dev:' after the conditional bpf_test_run call and before the comment explaining xdp_buff conversion.
intent_record.how: This label creates a jump target for goto statements, enabling controlled cleanup flow. Code that needs to release netdevice references can now jump to this label to ensure proper resource cleanup even when errors occur, rather than skipping the xdp_buff conversion logic.

commit a6763080856f444868620ae065ac25cbac0c4922
Author: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date:   Wed Feb 2 21:53:20 2022 +0100

    bpf: test_run: Fix OOB access in bpf_prog_test_run_xdp
    
    Fix the following kasan issue reported by syzbot:
    
    BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in __skb_frag_set_page include/linux/skbuff.h:3242 [inline]
    BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in bpf_prog_test_run_xdp+0x10ac/0x1150 net/bpf/test_run.c:972
    Write of size 8 at addr ffff888048c75000 by task
bic_trace_step.reason: The function shows the fix is already present. At line 1002, xdp_convert_buff_to_md(&xdp, ctx) is called BEFORE the error check at line 1003 (if (ret)). The comment at lines 998-1001 explicitly explains this: 'We convert the xdp_buff back to an xdp_md before checking the return code so the reference count of any held netdevice will be decremented even if the test run failed.' This ensures that xdp_convert_buff_to_md() is called on all paths after xdp_convert_md_to_buff() (line 953), including error paths at lines 967, 973, and 986 which jump to 'out' label. The vulnerable construct (skipping xdp_convert_buff_to_md() on error paths) is NOT present in this code - the fix has already been applied.

Examining the diff, the new code path for live packet mode (do_live=true) calls bpf_test_run_xdp_live() at line 1316, which internally calls xdp_test_run_batch() and xdp_test_run_teardown(). However, the critical issue is that xdp_convert_buff_to_md() is only called at lines 1319-1320 AFTER the test run completes. In the error paths within bpf_test_run_xdp_live() (specifically in xdp_test_run_setup() at lines 145-167 where multiple error labels exist: err_mmodel, err_pp, err_skbs), if setup fails, the function returns early without ever reaching xdp_convert_buff_to_md(). Additionally, if xdp_test_run_batch() returns an error (line 1315), the code still proceeds to xdp_convert_buff_to_md(), but the vulnerability description indicates there are error paths that skip this call entirely. The diff shows the vulnerable construct is present: error handling in xdp_test_run_setup() can return without proper cleanup of device references, and the fix (ensuring xdp_convert_buff_to_md() is always called) is not yet implemented in this commit.
